PullRequest.Title: agents: preserve session identity on first send
PullRequest.Body:
agents: preserve session identity on first send

The first-send path could replace a new remote session with an unrelated archived session.
A catalogue refresh could discover that old session before the requested session appeared.
The novelty fallback then selected the old session as the committed draft. The message still
ran in the requested session, but the visible conversation switched to the wrong session.

- Require the requested raw session ID and resource scheme in both the cache and session-added
  notification paths. Do not select a session only because it was absent from the earlier cache.
- Remove the novelty snapshot, in-flight own-ID set, and committed-ID claim set. Keep cancellation
  and connection-loss handling.
- Add tests for newly discovered archived and unarchived sessions in both matching paths.
- Update first-send test mocks to materialize the requested session ID.

Why the fallback and in-flight bookkeeping can be removed safely:

- The original novelty matcher came from #307732, when drafts used temporary untitled URIs.
  #313622 later made the client create the session URI and added a guard that rejects a backend
  URI different from the requested URI. First-send commitment therefore preserves identity.
- Commit 87d66b3a18fecc3f134f57467466203abee4e704 (#324792) preferred the own ID but retained a
  novelty fallback "for backends that assign a fresh id." That rationale does not match the
  first-send creation contract now enforced by the handler.
- The in-flight own-ID set protected the fallback from selecting another concurrent draft's
  session. Exact matching removes that possibility: send A accepts only A, even when B appears
  first. The claim set is also unnecessary for distinct drafts because their matches cannot
  overlap. Backend identity remapping would require an explicit mapping, not a novelty guess.
- The existing concurrent-send regression remains and passes: B materializes before A, and
  each send commits to its own session. Cached own-session and delayed-materialization tests
  also pass.

Validation:

- Client transpilation passed.
- Complete local and remote provider suites: 392 passing, 11 pending.
- ESLint passed for all three changed files.
- git diff --check passed.
- No live remote UI end-to-end validation was performed.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337322

Scenarios.Scenario: First message sent from a new local or remote agent-host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The send waits for draft configuration/eager creation, loads the chat model, dispatches the message through IChatService, then awaits _refreshSessions/listSessions and resolves the committed session from the cache or a session-added event. The diff keeps the post-send listSessions boundary on the critical path but replaces the former cache snapshot and full-cache fallback scan with an exact Map lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the first chat request to the selected agent-host-backed chat participant through IChatService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per user first-send action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IChatService.sendRequest call occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The message dispatch must complete before commitment waiting starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List all local agent-host sessions through the MessagePort-proxied IAgentConnection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One awaited post-send listing per first send; on an uninitialized cache the diff may remove one additional pre-send listing previously launched by _ensureSessionCache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The post-send listing was already present, and the old pre-send cache initialization could add another listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The post-send listing must complete before the immediate exact cache check; otherwise the waiter continues via notifications.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List all sessions through the remote agent-host connection for a remote provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One awaited post-send listing per remote first send, with the same possible reduction of a cold pre-send listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote listSessions round trip was already performed after sending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The remote round trip remains on the commitment critical path exactly as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The session catalogue size controls refresh reconciliation cost. The removed Set construction and fallback scan previously added O(number of cached sessions) CPU/allocation per first send; the new exact lookup is O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single send performs one awaited post-send refresh. Independent concurrent sends can still issue independent listSessions calls because _refreshSessions is not coalesced, but that behavior predates the diff; removing the pre-send _ensureSessionCache call can eliminate an additional cold-cache refresh rather than increase concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With a warm cache, the requested raw ID is checked directly after refresh. With a cold/uninitialized cache, the old code could start a pre-send refresh through _ensureSessionCache and then start the existing post-send refresh; the new code only performs the post-send refresh. Empty and failed refresh behavior remains owned by the existing authoritative-cache and retry logic.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk directly deletes the Set copy, fallback cache scan, and pre-send cache initialization while retaining the same post-send refresh call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalogue sizes and local/remote round-trip durations vary, but the direction of the changed CPU, allocation, and boundary counts is non-increasing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed path reduces cache-sized CPU/allocation and may reduce cold-cache IPC/network work while preserving the existing mandatory send and refresh boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Concurrent first sends while same-type and archived sessions are discovered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each send dispatches independently, performs its existing post-send catalogue refresh, then waits for only its own scheme/raw-ID match. Unrelated cached sessions and notification batches are inspected locally but no longer qualify through novelty fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch each first message to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per concurrent send, so k dispatches for k independently initiated drafts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-draft dispatch fan-out existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each corresponding send must finish before that draft starts commitment matching.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the full session catalogue with listSessions for each waiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to k overlapping post-send listings for k concurrent sends; catalogue reconciliation is per listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each waiter already called _refreshSessions; the diff removes auxiliary pre-send cache initialization rather than adding refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each waiter awaits its own refresh before checking the cache and subscribing for later additions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of concurrent first sends and the number of sessions in each refresh result. Notification matching scales with the size of each added batch. The diff changes cache matching from a full catalogue scan (and potentially two event-array scans) to one exact cache lookup and one event-array find.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: For k concurrent sends, up to k chat dispatches and k post-send listSessions operations may overlap; there is no shared refresh coalescing in this path. This concurrency existed before the diff, and the removed pre-send initialization cannot increase it. Each waiter owns a DisposableStore that is released on exact match, cancellation, connection loss, or provider disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every waiter checks the refreshed cache by its own raw ID, so warm discoveries resolve immediately and unrelated positive cache entries are ignored. Misses remain pending for a matching notification; failed refreshes follow existing retry behavior. Removed claim and in-flight ID sets decrease temporary retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the tests and production call flow establish independent waiters, exact ID matching, existing per-send refreshes, and deterministic listener disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large bursts of simultaneous drafts are uncommon and catalogue sizes are product-dependent, but neither uncertainty affects the before/after conclusion that no work or concurrency was added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Exact matching removes fallback scans and temporary ownership sets; existing uncoalesced per-send boundary fan-out is not introduced or materially amplified by this PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. The production change is performance-neutral to beneficial: it removes O(catalogue-size) snapshot/scan work, temporary ID retention, and a possible cold-cache refresh without adding boundary calls, eager work, or longer-lived resources. Test-only changes add bounded fixtures and assertions and do not affect product runtime.
